title: Fallback Strategies Slate + Operator Shortcuts
content:
Purpose:
Quick, operational-focused sketch for the Rollouts Wizard that prioritizes fast fallback and operator shortcuts. This doc is a working slate: not final UX, contains microcopy tests, failure-mode notes, and a prioritized backlog aimed at reducing time-to-recover for on-call engineers and product operators.

Context / Why this matters:
- Observability and smart fallback exist, but operators still spend too long debugging before shifting traffic.
- For high-throughput customers we need a 30s to safe-fallback path; current flows are 2–5 minutes in practice.
- Goal: make rollback/fallback decisions discoverable, reversible, and automatable from the same compact surface where you define canary/A-B rules.

Audience:
- SRE & on-call engineers who run incident mitigation
- Product/platform owners who run canary or A/B experiments
- Console operators who need low-friction guardrails during peak load or model regression

High-level constraints:
- Must not require writing policy language. Non-dev operators should be able to trigger safe-fallbacks.
- Preserve audit trail; all operator actions logged and linkable to incidents.
- Provide immediate preview of downstream cost/latency tradeoffs when fallback is applied.

User stories (prioritized):
1) As an on-call, I want a single-click fall back to a compatible model variant with a toggle to keep canary traffic for diagnostics, so I can reduce error rate immediately.
2) As PM, I want the wizard to suggest fallback targets (smaller model, quantized variant, regional replica) based on runbook heuristics so operators have safe options.
3) As operator, I want keyboard shortcuts and a compact CLI-style quick-panel so I can act without switching context.
4) As auditor, I want a compact summary of what changed and link to the incident for postmortem.

Compact flows (sketch descriptions) — aim for one-screen action when possible:
A) Fast-Fallback Panel (default collapsed in rollout editor)
- Top row: status pill (Healthy / Degraded / Stalled) + quick health summary (5s latency p95, error spike %)
- Primary action: "Initiate Safe Fallback" (keyboard: / then f) opens modal with three prefilled options: Compatible Variant, Lower-capacity Tier, Region-only routing. Each option shows delta in p99 latency and estimated cost per 10k tokens.
- Secondary: "Keep 10% canary for telemetry" checkbox. Default: true for experiments, false for production routes.
- Microcopy under actions: "Fallback is reversible. Telemetry persists for canary slices."

B) Canary Pause & Snapshot
- When pausing canary, capture a snapshot of recent prompt set and example anomalous outputs (auto-populated top 5 failing prompts).
- Snapshot saved to linkable artifact (postmortem anchor).

C) Auto-Fallback Policy Composer (lightweight DSL w/ templated rules)
- Templated rules: "If error-rate > X for Y minutes" / "If p95 latency > L for Z minutes and throughput < T".
- Templates expose parameters via sliders (no code).
- Preview button runs simulated traffic for last 60m and shows % of requests that would have triggered fallback.

Operator Shortcuts (keyboard + micro-UI):
- / f : open fast-fallback modal
- / p : pause canary
- / s : snapshot current canary traffic + top anomalous examples
- Alt + enter : apply policy immediately (bypass confirm for admins)
- Quick panel accessible via Cmd+K "Rollouts quick actions"; support natural language commands like: "fallback to 4bit-gpt-compat and keep 5%". Prototype uses fuzzy match, not full NL parsing.

Wireframe annotations (visual cues, non-visual text):
- Use a single-row compact header for each rollout with small pills showing current traffic routing and active safety policies. Hover reveals a micro-timeline (++ to expand).
- Visual severity color scale (green/amber/red) but also numeric summaries for colorblind accessibility.
- Confirmation modal emphasizes reversibility rather than irreversibility: headline "Switch traffic to fallback (reversible)"; second line: "We will re-route X% of traffic to model Y. Telemetry retained for diagnostics."

Failure-mode matrix (short):
- Fallback target incompatible (e.g., different tokenizer): show immediate compatibility warning and disable one-click fallback; provide two-step migration checklist.
- Fallback increases latency/cost: UI highlights whether fallback reduces or increases p99 and shows estimated cost delta. If cost increases, require typed confirmation.
- Partial-region failures: pre-populate region routing option with affected regions.

Backlog (candidate tickets) — rough prioritization:
- UI-1: Fast-Fallback modal P0 (keyboard shortcuts, default options, telemetry toggle) — target sprint +1
- UI-2: Snapshot capture + artifact link P1 — attach to incident flow
- UI-3: Policy templating + slider params P1 — include simulation preview
- UI-4: Microcopy A/B test suite (two header variants + confirm copy) P2
- UI-5: Accessibility pass and colorblind checks P1

Open questions / undecided items (to resolve in grooming):
- Default for "keep canary": should it be true for experiments and false for production routes? (ops vs PM preference)
- How aggressive should automated suggestion ranking be? (safety vs speed tradeoff)
- Where to persist snapshots (Confluence vs internal artifact store)? Cost/retention implications.

Mini acceptance criteria (for first usable iteration):
- One-click fallback to a verified compatible variant with telemetry retention completed in <30s on staging env (manual test).
- Keyboard shortcuts wired to open/close fast-fallback modal.
- Fallback actions emit audit events with links to snapshot artifact and incident id.

Notes / scratch ideas (quick bullets):
- Consider a "panic mode" keyboard combo that automatically applies the top-ranked fallback and emails the on-call rotation.
- Use existing Optimize signals to surface recommended fallback (e.g., quantized variant that historically reduces cost with small quality delta).
- Small visual affordance: animate traffic-shift bar for 3s to help operator watch traffic move.

Next steps:
- Sync with SRE (Ethan) on requirements for audit events and snapshot retention (this week).
- Quick prototype of modal (Figma): Rina to produce 2 variants by 2026-02-05.
- Groom backlog with PM + SRE; decide default keep-canary behavior.

Referenced tickets / threads (for migration into Jira/Confluence):
- JIRA-PROD-4321 (Fallback modal prototype)
- slack: #rollouts-ops: thread "panic-mode sketch" (pinned)

End of slate — this is intentionally terse and operator-oriented. Use this doc as the working place to collect short experiments before drafting a longer playbook.
